title: Three commits on main that should have been on a branch
intro: You've been coding for an hour and just noticed you never created a branch: your three commits are sitting on your local main. Nothing is pushed. main is a protected branch, so the push would be rejected anyway, and you need the work on a feature branch for a pull request.

steps.prompt: Confirm the situation: show how your main compares with origin/main.
steps.fake_output:
On branch main
Your branch is ahead of 'origin/main' by 3 commits.
  (use "git push" to publish your local commits)

nothing to commit, working tree clean
steps.hint: git status tells you how far ahead of the remote you are.

steps.prompt: Save the work first: create a branch called feature/export-csv pointing at your current commit (don't switch to it yet).
steps.fake_output: (no output: feature/export-csv now points at your 3 commits)
steps.hint: git branch <name> creates a branch at the current commit without switching.

steps.prompt: Now move main back to where the remote is, discarding nothing that matters (the commits are safe on the new branch).
steps.fake_output: HEAD is now at b7c8d9e Merge pull request #213
steps.hint: git reset --hard origin/main makes local main match the remote.

steps.prompt: Switch to feature/export-csv and carry on.
Check the three commits are on the branch and not on main: list commits on your branch that main doesn't have.
steps.fake_output:
9f2c1e7 Add CSV export endpoint
5d6e7f8 Add CSV serializer
a1b2c3d Add export permission check
steps.hint: A..B lists commits in B that aren't in A.

resolution: A branch is only a name pointing at a commit, so 'moving commits to another branch' needs no copying: create a new name at the current commit, then move the old name back. The order matters. Branch first, reset second: if you had reset main first, the commits would have had no branch pointing at them (still recoverable from the reflog, but needlessly scary). 'git reset --hard' was safe here only because the working tree was clean and the commits had another name. Prevention: protect main on the server so a push can't succeed, and set 'pull.ff only' so a diverged main is noticed quickly. Some people also show the current branch in their shell prompt, which removes most of these moments.
